practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the composition of the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 81 of the Constitution deals with the composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha). Article 79 is about the Constitution of Parliament, Article 80 is about the composition of the Rajya Sabha, and Article 85 deals with sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as originally envisaged by the Constitution, prior to recent amendments?
practiceQuestions.sol: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha was fixed at 552, which included up to 530 members from the states, up to 20 members from the Union Territories, and not more than 2 members of the Anglo-Indian community (nominated by the President).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act abolished the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, formally ended the special provision for nominating two members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha while extending reservation for SCs and STs.

practiceQuestions.q: At present, what is the total sanctioned strength (current maximum capacity) of the Lok Sabha following the removal of Anglo-Indian reserved seats?
practiceQuestions.sol: With the discontinuation of the 2 Anglo-Indian seats via the 104th Amendment, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha stands reduced from 552 to 550 (530 from states + 20 from UTs).

practiceQuestions.q: Members of the Lok Sabha are elected by which method of voting?
opts: Proportional Representation by means of Single Transferable Vote
Direct election on the basis of adult suffrage
Indirect election by State Legislative Assemblies
Nomination by the President of India
practiceQuestions.sol: Representatives of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people of India on the basis of universal adult suffrage using the First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) system.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum age required to contest an election to the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 84(b) of the Constitution, a person must be not less than 25 years of age to be qualified to fill a seat in the Lok Sabha. (For Rajya Sabha, it is 30 years).

practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article are seats in the Lok Sabha allocated to the states based on their population?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 81(1)(a) mandates that not more than 530 members shall be chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the states, allocated in such a way that the ratio between the population of each state and the number of seats is, as far as practicable, the same for all states.

practiceQuestions.q: Which body is empowered to conduct the delimitation of parliamentary constituencies after every census?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 82, Parliament enacts a Delimitation Act after every census. The Delimitation Commission, a high-power body, is set up to redraw constituency boundaries and fix seat counts.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act froze the allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha and the division of each state into territorial constituencies till the year 2000 based on the 1971 census?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 froze the Lok Sabha seat allocation based on the 1971 census till the year 2000 to encourage population control measures.

practiceQuestions.q: The 84th Amendment Act of 2001 extended the freeze on Lok Sabha seat allocation and territorial constituencies until which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 extended the ban on readjustment of Lok Sabha constituencies up to the year 2026 (based on the 1971 census), which was later reaffirmed by the 87th Amendment Act, 2003.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does Article 81 ensure that the ratio between the population of each state and the number of seats allotted to it is, as far as practicable, the same across all states?
opts: To guarantee proportional geographical representation rather than demographic representation
To ensure uniform political representation per capita across different states, maintaining democratic equity
To restrict the total number of MPs from crossing the constitutional cap of 600
To enable the Election Commission to easily alter state boundaries without parliamentary approval
practiceQuestions.sol: This principle ensures the principle of 'one vote, one value' in demographic terms across states, preventing citizens of smaller or larger states from experiencing disproportionate voting power per capita in the lower house.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the rationale behind enacting the 84th and 87th Constitutional Amendments that froze seat readjustment till 2026?
opts: To penalize southern states for failing to achieve high economic growth rates
To prevent states that successfully implemented population control policies from being penalized with a reduction in their Lok Sabha seat share
To allow the Supreme Court to directly oversee the delimitation process every ten years
To eliminate the need for Union Territories to have parliamentary representation

If readjustment had occurred based on contemporary census data prior to 2026, states that performed poorly on population stabilization would have gained more Lok Sabha seats, penalizing states that successfully managed population growth.

practiceQuestions.q: How are seats in the Lok Sabha distributed among Union Territories?
opts: Directly specified in the Constitution itself under a rigid schedule
Determined by Parliament through law (specifically the Union Territories (Direct Election to the House of the People) Act, 1965)
Appointed exclusively by the President of India based on cabinet recommendations
Proportional to the annual Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue generated by each Union Territory

While Article 81(1)(b) sets the upper ceiling of 20 members for Union Territories, the exact allocation of seats is prescribed by Parliament via legislation (such as the Union Territories (Direct Election to the House of the People) Act, 1965).

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional provision safeguards the representation of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 330 of the Constitution provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha in proportion to their respective populations in the state or union territory.

practiceQuestions.q: What does the 'First-Past-The-Post' (FPTP) system used in Lok Sabha elections imply?
opts: A candidate must secure more than 50% of the total valid votes polled to win
The candidate who wins the maximum number of votes among all contestants, even without an absolute majority, is declared elected
Seats are distributed among political parties strictly based on their vote share percentage
Only candidates nominated by national political parties can contest elections

India follows the plurality system (FPTP) for Lok Sabha elections, where the winning candidate simply needs to secure more votes than any individual opponent, regardless of whether they cross 50% of the vote share.

practiceQuestions.q: How are seats allocated among states for the Lok Sabha based on the principle of territorial constituencies?
opts: Every state is given an equal number of seats irrespective of its population size
Each state is divided into territorial constituencies such that the ratio of state population to seats is uniform across states
Seats are allocated purely based on the industrial output index of each state
Seats are assigned by the Prime Minister's Office based on political convenience

Article 81 mandates that each state is allotted a number of seats in the Lok Sabha in such a manner that the ratio between its population and the number of seats is consistent across states, preserving democratic proportionality.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies compiles the final Delimitation Order, and what is its legal status regarding judicial review?
opts: The Supreme Court of India; it can be challenged in any court.
The Delimitation Commission; its orders have the force of law and cannot be called in question in any court.
The Election Commission of India; it can be modified by state legislative assemblies.
